gap: No result ChatGPT got states that GOOLOO sells three different units under the 'A3' name at gooloo.com: the A3 Lite 2500A at $59.99, the A3 3000A at $69.99 and the A3 Pro 3000A at $89.99. ChatGPT's $89.99 'A3 3000A' card matches the A3 Pro's price, not the A3's. GOOLOO's A3 listing gives only a 5V/2A USB-C port, while WOLFBOX's MegaVolt16 Air has 65 W USB-C. WOLFBOX also says its own replacement jump-starter clamps are not compatible with its air-compressor jump starters.
standout_why: I opened the TechGearLab MegaVolt16 Air review (cited), gearmyride.com and autoboosting.com. TechGearLab covers only the MegaVolt16 Air: 8 L gas, 6 L diesel, 65 W USB, 1.3 h recharge. It does not mention 12 V/24 V, battery chemistry or boost voltage. Gearmyride lists the 'GOOLOO A3' as 9.0 L gas, 6.5 L diesel, 12 V and 150 PSI, but its USB-C entry says only 'USB device charging only'. It does not separate the A3, A3 Lite and A3 Pro. Autoboosting does not mention the A3 or the MegaVolt16 Air, and neither page mentions WOLFBOX's clamp exclusion. I could not open Popular Mechanics, which ChatGPT cited for the A3 (the fetch was blocked), so it may already separate the A3 variants. That is why the score is 2, not 3.
decides: This confirms the GOOLOO A3 as the value pick, but the shopper needs the exact model. The plain A3 is $69.99 at gooloo.com today and covers 12 V vehicles up to 9.0 L gas or 6.5 L diesel. The $89.99 card ChatGPT showed is the price of the A3 Pro, a different unit. If the shopper wants fast USB-C recharging or uses the pack as a power bank, the MegaVolt16 Air ($179.40 at wolfbox.com, 65 W USB-C per TechGearLab) is the better match. The A3 listing names only a 5V/2A USB-C port. For trucks with engines over 9.0 L gas or 6.5 L diesel, the MegaVolt 24Air is rated to 10 L gas and 10 L diesel.
